title: Orsen and the Debt
premise: Ada Joubert, a disgraced intelligence analyst erased from three agencies' rolls, survives on deniable casework until a client asks her to trace Flight 4471 — a plane that landed with every passenger manifest, radar log, and booking record scrubbed from existence mid-flight. Digging through paper trails and half-remembered contacts, Ada discovers the flight carried a stolen decryption key meant to trigger a refinery disaster staged as mechanical failure, and that her own erased past is tangled in the plot: the man who built the wipe is Orsen, her former handler and the only person who ever loved her. Torn between duty to stop the attack and the truth that exposing it means destroying Orsen, Ada races a countdown she can't fully see. In the end she stops the attack by feeding Orsen's own memory-wipe protocol back onto him, erasing their shared history so he can be captured without betraying her — leaving Ada free, invisible again, and grieving someone who no longer remembers why he loved her.
about_author: Rafael Vasquez is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade inside the paperwork of companies that preferred not to exist. He writes thrillers about people trapped in systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Unattributable
chapters.summary: Ada Joubert's POV. Working from a rented office above a laundromat, Ada takes a case from a lawyer who won't give his client's name: find out what happened aboard Flight 4471. The beat is weary competence — she's good at work no one wants signed.

chapters.title: Nothing in the Air
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Every digital record of 4471 is gone: manifests, radar archives, even the airline's own schedules. Only a printed boarding stub in the lawyer's possession proves the flight happened. Beat: cold dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Paper Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She works analog — airport janitors, a fueling contractor's carbon copies — and reconstructs eleven passengers, one of whom boarded under a name that matches a dead man. Beat: the thrill of the hunt reawakening.

chapters.title: Three Agencies Ago
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Her last day at her second agency, when she flagged an anomaly and was quietly erased for it; her handler Orsen chose the institution over her. Beat: betrayal remembered as love's first wound.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The dead-man passenger was Marcus Vey, a cryptographer whose obituary predates his boarding pass. His sister confirms he feared 'a cleanup crew that edits reality.' Beat: the case turns personal and dangerous.

chapters.title: Orsen
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finds Orsen's signature in the wipe methodology — elegant, unmistakable, hers once upon a time. He taught her everything; now he's erasing the crime she's chasing. Beat: vertigo of hunting the man who made her.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Orsen, watching Ada's investigation through old taps, debates whether to warn or destroy her; Ada sets a trap using a contact channel only he would recognize. Beat: two predators circling an old intimacy.

chapters.title: Coffee, No Names
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They meet in a train-station café, trading courtesies sharpened into threats. He offers her reinstatement and silence; she refuses. Beat: love against duty, spoken entirely in subtext.

chapters.title: What Vey Carried
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reconstructing Vey's luggage claim, she finds he couriered a hardware decryption key — capable of overriding industrial safety interlocks remotely. Target: the Calvert Point refinery. Beat: the abstract becomes catastrophic.

chapters.title: Scheduled Accident
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Maintenance logs show Calvert Point's inspection cycle was manipulated months ago; the attack will read as corrosion failure, killing hundreds and gutting investigations. Beat: horror at how clean the design is.

chapters.title: Burned Again
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Someone leaks her location; a cleanup team ransacks her office. She escapes with Vey's sister and a single backup drive. Beat: fear and fury — invisibility has failed her completely.

chapters.title: The Sister's Testimony
chapters.summary: Vey's sister Lena's POV. She reveals Marcus left her a sealed letter: if anything happened to him, the key's true destination wasn't the refinery — the refinery is cover for stealing the response teams' communications. Beat: the plot deepens and doubles.

chapters.title: Orsen's Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Through an encrypted message he admits the wipe was commissioned above him, that he took the job partly to keep Ada's name out of the operation, and that he no longer controls the timeline. Beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown Without a Clock
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cross-referencing refinery shift rotations and a decommissioned emergency drill, she narrows the strike window to a 36-hour span beginning Friday night. Beat: relentless momentum, exhaustion transmuted into focus.

chapters.title: The Man Above Orsen
chapters.summary: Ada and Lena's POV. They identify the commissioner: Deputy Director Hale, who once erased Ada and now needs the attack to bury a bribery scandal. Beat: righteous anger — the system isn't broken, it's working as designed.

chapters.title: Offer She Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Hale's POV then Ada's. Hale offers Ada full reinstatement and Vey's posthumous exoneration if she delivers the key and disappears. Beat: temptation laid bare — the same bargain Orsen once refused to make for her.

chapters.title: The Key Is Already There
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She realizes the key never left the refinery: Vey hid it inside the plant's own calibration lab before boarding. The attack team must retrieve it on-site. Beat: the trap inverts — they're walking into her ground.

chapters.title: Friday Night
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The retrieval team infiltrates; Ada, tipped by Orsen, shadows them through the calibration lab as sirens begin their scripted test. Beat: breathless cat-and-mouse among the machinery of the fake accident.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Orsen intercepts his own team to buy Ada minutes, choosing her over the institution for the first time; she reaches the key seconds before the override initiates. Beat: sacrifice as the truest confession.

chapters.title: The Wipe Turned Inward
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV. Cornered by Hale's men with the attack still armed, Ada triggers Orsen's own memory-edit protocol on him — erasing every record of their shared history so his capture can't lead back to her, and so he dies to his old self willingly. Beat: devastating cost of victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hale falls to Lena's sealed letter and Ada's anonymized dossier; the refinery stands; Orsen, detained, looks at Ada with polite blankness and asks if they've met. Beat: hollow triumph, grief without a grave.

chapters.title: Invisible, On Purpose
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She declines reinstatement, burns her remaining files, and takes a new unattributable case — but keeps one item: a coffee receipt from the train station, dated the day they met. Beat: quiet, chosen solitude; identity reclaimed on her own terms.
